blocks.text: Twin and Close — the founding wave

content.value: The Heggemsnes Act's second arc opens here: upgrade Barkpark Papers to the standard of an unconstrained Fable artifact, honestly, with screenshots as evidence. Wave 1 ports the Eight-Minute Erasure artifact into a real Paper, measures every pixel where the Paper loses, fixes what is systemic, and turns the friction log into the agent-authoring onramp.

items.label: block types the renderer already speaks (asciicast, chart, diagram, diff, filetree among them)

content.value: “We need every evidence — every detail — a true honest analysis — we will spend this time to upgrade our paper system to the next level — we will figure out how we can improve the aesthetics of the paper — by utilizing image analysis — comparing to what a Fable agent would make if it wasn't as constrained — we will call this the Heggemsnes Act — a declaration of humility in front of the people who want to help out. Also — we want to make sure that agents are a lot better at writing papers when they get into Barkpark — for example — I often see agents trying to create their own HTML etc — and not utilizing the system — the paper you just made should be something our Barkpark paper should learn from.”

The benchmark artifact is an editorial evidence page: a display serif title at enormous scale with one accent-colored italic word, a four-stop timeline strip under the ingress, dual serif/mono registers, a red/green accent discipline where color always means something (erasure vs. verification), labeled sequence-diagram and timeline SVGs, embedded replayable terminal casts, verdict tables, and stat tiles with per-trial dots — tuned in both light and dark.

The current reader, screenshotted today on /papers/heggemsnes-act at 1200px, is competent but flat by comparison: the title renders small, the text column hugs the left with a dead right margin holding three floating mode buttons, body text is justified and hyphenated into a cramped measure, stat tiles are flat gray boxes, and the paper's 'notes' block — the five executed remedies, the heart of the Act — renders as blank lines: the ingest wall accepted plain-string items that the renderer silently drops. That is a live defect on the doctrine paper itself.

The sharpest structural finding: the renderer's block vocabulary is far richer than anyone uses. Fifty-six types exist in the render modules — asciicast, terminal, chart, heatmap, diagram, diff, filetree, duel, pipeline, roadmap — while live papers use roughly ten. The gap to the artifact is therefore only partly missing capability; it is mostly (a) the aesthetic quality of what renders and (b) discoverability: agents cannot see the deck from where they author, so they hand-roll HTML instead.

Wave 1 builds the instrument and spends it in the same motion. Port the Eight-Minute Erasure artifact into a genuine Paper — the twin — using only the existing block deck, logging every point where the deck cannot express the artifact or where the author is tempted toward raw HTML. Screenshot twin against artifact, both themes, two widths. Every pixel where the twin falls short of the artifact becomes a named, screenshotable defect in a ranked gap ledger — with each gap classified SYSTEMIC (typography scale, measure, palette, stat tiles — fixes every one of ~747 papers) or BESPOKE (a one-off device that becomes a block proposal for a later wave). Wave 1 builders close only the systemic half, through the token manifest, gated by the view-edit-parity audit and a fixed regression panel of existing papers re-screenshotted before and after.
Author the erasure artifact as a Paper with today's deck; the friction log is a first-class deliverable.
Image analysis of twin vs. artifact: measured observations (type scale, measure, contrast, spacing), not vibes; every gap ranked and classified systemic vs. bespoke.
Renderer/CSS fixes for the top systemic gaps — editorial type scale, column and measure, justification policy, stat tiles, notes defect, theme polish — with before/after screenshots.
Turn the friction log into the first agent-authoring onramp: a canonical premium-paper guide and sharper bp CLI door copy, so the paper door beats hand-rolled HTML.

Rival B — Door first: ship the agent onramp (bp paper scaffold, error copy, guide) before touching aesthetics. Rejected as the opener: an onramp that leads agents to papers which still lose to their own hand-rolled HTML teaches them the door is not worth taking; the incentive to bypass survives. The epic's own first acceptance criterion is the screenshot-grounded gap analysis, and the onramp gets strictly better material once the twin's friction log exists.

Rival C — Direct glow-up: start restyling render.ex and the reader CSS by taste, no instrument. Fastest visible change, but it abandons the wish's spine — every evidence, true honest analysis, image analysis against the unconstrained benchmark — and leaves later waves nothing repeatable to measure against.

Sharpest attack on the winner: overfitting. The erasure page is one bespoke incident record; optimizing until the twin matches it could bolt one-off devices onto the renderer and regress 747 papers built for the current look. The wave absorbs this three ways: the systemic/bespoke gate means wave 1 only ships changes that improve every paper; the regression panel re-screenshots a fixed sample of existing papers before merge; and the gap ledger demands measured observations so taste disputes resolve against numbers. A second attack — the ingest wall itself may refuse an artifact-scale paper (the 17th-heading and ~63KB 500s are already on file) — is absorbed by making wall limits a survey lane before any port begins.

blocks.text: Survey digest — what sixteen lanes established

content.value: The direction's description of today's reader is corrected in three places by measurement. The public paper column is CENTERED (.bp-paper-shell has margin: 0 auto; the article shell is 720px), nothing on the paper surface is justified (zero text-align: justify hits across the repo and the live pages), and only hyphenation is real (hyphens: auto on paragraphs, paper-surface.css:157). The left-hug impression comes from the Studio editor panel, which deliberately has no auto margins — a different surface. The gap ledger must name true causes, not inherited framing.

The crown candidate finding: the public reader almost certainly renders body prose at 16px while the token manifest says 18px. paper-surface.css defines --bp-body-size from the token but no rule in that file applies it to paragraphs; the only consumer of --bp-body-size is Studio's root.html.heex. Two surveyors' live measurements disagree — 16px/26.4 on a body paragraph versus 20.48px/30.72 — but 20.48px is exactly the ingress rule's 1.28rem, so the second measurement very likely landed on an ingress, not body prose. Verifier v1 settles the number; it is the before column of every typography row in the gap ledger.

The renderer's vocabulary is confirmed rich and unused: 754 published papers carry 79 block types, the top ten types are 96.1 percent of all 36,150 top-level blocks, and only three deck types (duel, lineage, field-number) appear in zero papers. The ingest wall has NO block-type allowlist anywhere — a live probe published asciicast + terminal end to end with ordinary credentials, and unknown types render a visible Unsupported placeholder (four published papers are broken that way today: spacer x13, code_block, codeBlock). The same permissiveness is the root of the notes defect.

Notes-defect anatomy is settled at file:line. The renderer drop site is Components.note_item_html (components.ex:495) — deliberately guard-free for byte-fidelity, so a plain-string item emits an empty 4px row. The wall's real shape gate is BlockOps.validate_render_shapes (block_ops.ex:1487), which is type-keyed with arms only for list and table; its catch-all recurses blocks/children and never looks at items, so every items-bearing widget (notes, cards, pipeline) is unguarded. The briefed attribution to the hollow guard was wrong — hollow.ex counts bare strings AS content. The fix is two-ended (wall arm plus renderer contract) and cross-surface: notes has TUI goldens. The wall/renderer key divergence (Hollow accepts text|value|title|caption; the inline renderer reads only value) is the same false-green class, proven live by a paper that published 200 with body_html_len=0.

Doctrine and wall state: the spacing doctrine has REVERSED — /papers/mechanical-spacing-doctrine is now the Reader-Owned Spacing Doctrine, empty-paragraph spacers are forbidden and 351 were purged; the user's global CLAUDE.md and this workflow's own boilerplate still carry the retired law, and this digest was authored spacer-free accordingly. The 17-heading 500 is FIXED on origin/main with a regression test. The ~63KB publish 500 has NO code source anywhere in api/lib (the only body limit is 100MB) — it is unlocated folklore until verifier v4 reproduces or refutes it. The epic-quality caps (80 blocks, 16 headings, 5000 words, no spacers) bind ONLY papers tagged epic-cycle-wave-paper; an untagged twin passes the wall with just description + registered weighted tags.

The agent-authoring door is measured and damning: bp onramp output mentions papers ZERO times across all four targets; the capabilities manifest has no paper noun and its single authoring line advertises an HTML payload — the bypass is invited, not merely permitted; bp paper is read-only with no pointer to the write door; the only authoring doc is a 32-line human-tier cheatsheet the router never loads. Two committed hand-rolled HTML spec deliverables (426KB and 17KB) are the fossil record of this failure.

One live contradiction between lanes: erasure-anatomy classed the artifact's four-stop clock strip as a missing block, while figure-chart found that `lineage` is a purpose-built horizontal dated-node strip (auto-fit grid, overline/title/body/value/source slots) and that `chart` already carries a full verdict-annotation layer (regions, refLines, points, four tones) that nobody uses. Two of three lanes missed lineage entirely — itself evidence for the discoverability thesis. Verifier v3 renders the proof in pixels. Also established: font stacks already match the benchmark artifact; the real deltas are display scale (artifact h1 is 2.6x ours), the missing wide band (--wide 1040px has no counterpart — every block is capped at the 640px text column), verdict accent tokens, hyphenation, and numeric table discipline.

blocks.text: Verification results — ten probes, four refutations

content.value: Ten verifiers ran between the digest and this plan; every assignment reported, so no deficit shapes the cut. Four premises died and each death reshaped a slice: the reader really renders body prose at 16px against an 18px token, the parity gate really is blind to one-sided CSS adds, lineage really is not a horizontal strip, and the 63KB ingest ceiling never existed.

rows.value: SETTLED: body prose computes 16px/26.4px in both themes while --bp-body-size resolves 18px with ZERO reader consumers; the earlier 20.48px reading was the ingress (1.28rem). Trap proven live: applying the token alone collapses the ingress/body ratio 1.28x to 1.14x because every role size is root-relative rem. Body CPL averages 84 at the 640px measure.

HOLE CONFIRMED: adding font-size to .bp-paper-surface p one-sided passed all 1,156 portable_doc tests, the paper-editor mirror and design/check.mjs — only a COLOR literal reds Part E. Shared-value changes and .bp-role-* adds DO red, so the gate architecture is asymmetric, and wave typography lands in the blind half.

lineage REFUTED as a strip: four stops wrap 3+1 at 720px with no spine element. Chart annotations all render, but tick text paints 4.26px at a 360 viewport, a last-index point label clips (bbox right 654 vs viewBox 640), and region tones are indistinguishable at opacity 0.08. Mermaid hydrates yet paints 3.73px labels at 360.

63KB ceiling REFUTED: 62,405 B, 63,740 B and 252,360 B all publish HTTP 200. The real cap is 5,000 first-pass words (plus 80 blocks / 16 headings), scoped to the exact tag epic-cycle-wave-paper; closed expandables are exempt. The 17-heading 500 is fixed — 422 with details.failures, printed by bp.

Exactly 2 papers carry malformed notes items, while 215 papers (28%) carry CANONICAL byline strings — so the wall arm must be type-keyed, never generic over items. 10 papers carry text-keyed inline leaves; 4 are 100% hollow behind 200s (deploy-reliability-wave-4 serves 226KB with 22 empty h2). Prior art cch-w57 is open and ADOPTED, not re-filed.

The 28-file benchmark archive sits at tooling/paper-excellence/evidence/, manifest-sealed and byte-identical to the originals; guerrilla equals origin/main (compile-time SHA plus verbatim-CSS containment). Caveat: the 20 baselines are fold-only 1x against the artifact full-page 2x.

A serverless, DB-less, networkless render is pixel-metric IDENTICAL to the live reader: 19/19 blocks byte-verbatim in the served page, CSS 154,732 B on both sides. The reader ETag is content plus a 7-day bucket — blind to renderer and CSS deploys — so any guerrilla-pointed rig must cold-fetch.

New type/measure tokens are nearly free but INERT: emit.mjs hand-enumerates its reading vars, and a letterSpacing leaf already in tokens.json is emitted NOWHERE. Teaching emit costs ~5 lines and regenerates exactly 2 artifacts with the mirror automatic. A COLOR token is the expensive kind — Part F reds it on sight. The built editor CSS ships stale with green CI.

An untagged twin passes the wall (caps are tag-scoped and would not bind: 11 headings, ~1,950 words). Nesting works on the reader — section grid 2-up, columns, expandable. container is NOT a block type: it renders Unsupported and silently DROPS its children. Grid span is a top-level child key; code blocks read only the value key.

The or-HTML-payload string is authored at bulldocs.ex:316 and duplicated in 5 files, one CI-gated (openapi drift). bp onramp mentions papers ZERO times across all targets. 31 of 764 papers (4.1%) are body_html-only — four authored in August — and an HTML-only table collapses to run-together text in the terminal reader.

content.value: Coverage: ten of ten verifiers reported — no deficit. Not-founds worth keeping: no prior Barkpark task or paper owns the reader-typography finding; no pixel-diff dependency or screenshot harness exists on main; no byte budget exists anywhere in the render path.
The charter (PR #11568, .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-epic-charter.md) is the epic memory; until that PR merges, this list is the readable copy of wave-1 law.
